skills.description: Using fixed cameras at home (living room, bedroom) of elderly people living alone, the system analyzes daily videos and detects negative behavior indicators during solo time: dazing (long-duration motionless gazing without purposeful action), sighing (rapid chest rise-and-fall with audible expiration), and self-talking (mouth movement without any conversation partner). It counts the frequency and duration of these behaviors and comprehensively evaluates the elder's emotional risk level (low / medium / high). The skill assists family members or community workers in understanding the elder's mental state and timely providing emotional care or psychological intervention. Application scenarios: homes of solo-living elders, nursing homes, community daycare centers. The system generates a daily emotional-risk report; when the risk level is 'medium' or 'high', it pushes reminders. Skill features: loneliness and depression in the elderly are common mental-health issues, and early behavioral signals are often overlooked. AI automatic monitoring of dazing / sighing / self-talking helps family members detect mental abnormalities early, intervene promptly, and improve the elder's quality of life.
